newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice ends sharply down in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice ends sharply down in active trading.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended sharply down in active trading on Wednesday with most investors offsetting their position, unwilling to taking delivery of physical goods for the September 1996 contract, traders said.

The September contract, which will start physical delivery on Tuesday next week, ended limit-down at 2,441 yuan ($293) per tonne, losing 97 yuan. It opened at 2,531 and hit a intra-day high of 2,552. The October contract fell 49 yuan to 2,326.
Combined volume rose sharply to 105,300 tonnes from 33,100.
Traders said September moved in a narrow range in early trading today before heavy selling made its price dive.
The open interest of the September contract plunged to 15,660 lots after Wednesday's trading from Tuesday's 25,670. One lot is five tonnes.
"The main factor was that long position holders did not want to deliver physical goods due to the low spot price," a trader said. Spot rice in Shanghai is now around 2,400 yuan per tonne.
Traders expected investors to continue to offset their positions before the delivery, helping push down futures prices in the short term.
